questionText: What is the difference between @Component and @Bean?

target.learningOutcome: The learner can contrast scan-based class registration with factory-method registration and choose the clearer form for one construction need.
outOfScope: Full and lite configuration proxy internals

claims.statement: Component marks a class as a candidate for scan-based bean definition registration, while Bean marks a factory method whose returned object is registered.
Beans registered through component scanning and Bean factory methods are both managed by the Spring container and can receive dependencies, scope, and lifecycle processing.
Using component stereotypes for natural application roles and Bean methods for explicit construction is useful guidance, not a framework rule based solely on code ownership.

examples.title: Scanned ReceiptService receives a Clock returned by a Bean factory method
